note: Every input property used by the flame simulation, with its source. Values copied from the sources named; per-kg values derived by dividing by the NIST molecular weight. Gas-phase thermochemistry and transport are computed by Cantera (see chem.py), not taken from this file.

sources.T_boil_K: NIST Chemistry WebBook, C142825, phase change: 371.5 +/- 0.3 K (average of 215 of 227 values) https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C142825&Mask=4
sources.h_fg_kJ_kg: NIST WebBook: dvapH 31.77 kJ/mol at 371.6 K (Majer and Svoboda, 1985), / 100.2019 g/mol
sources.rho_l_kg_m3: NIST WebBook fluid properties, isobar 0.101325 MPa, 295 K: 682.28 kg/m3
sources.cp_l_kJ_kgK: NIST WebBook fluid properties, isobar 0.101325 MPa, 295 K: 2.2347 J/g K

sources.T_boil_K: NIST WebBook C64175: 351.5 +/- 0.2 K (average of 138 of 148 values) https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C64175&Mask=4
sources.h_fg_kJ_kg: NIST WebBook: dvapH 38.56 kJ/mol at 351.5 K (Majer and Svoboda, 1985), / 46.0684 g/mol
sources.rho_l_kg_m3: PubChem CID 702, Density: 0.7893 g/cu cm at 20 C (CRC Handbook 95th ed., p. 3-246)
sources.cp_l_kJ_kgK: NIST WebBook C64175 condensed phase: Cp,liquid 112.4 J/mol K at 298.15 K (Petrov, Peshekhodov et al., 1989), / 46.0684

sources.T_boil_K: NIST WebBook C67561: 337.8 +/- 0.3 K (average of 154 of 171 values) https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C67561&Mask=4
sources.h_fg_kJ_kg: NIST WebBook: dvapH 35.21 kJ/mol at 337.7 K (Majer and Svoboda, 1985), / 32.0419 g/mol
sources.rho_l_kg_m3: NIST WebBook fluid properties, isobar 0.101325 MPa, 295 K: 789.28 kg/m3
sources.cp_l_kJ_kgK: NIST WebBook fluid properties, isobar 0.101325 MPa, 295 K: 2.5155 J/g K

gases_note: Methane, ethylene and propane are gases at cabin conditions, so no droplet values (K, B, burn-out time) are given for them: null. Their flames are modelled as a small gas-jet source.

lhv_reported_MJ_kg.source: Wikipedia 'Heat of combustion', table 'Lower heating value for some organic compounds (at 25 C)'; used only to cross-check the Cantera values

transport_added.note: Lennard-Jones parameters for species missing from gri30 transport, from the San Diego mechanism transport file https://web.eng.ucsd.edu/mae/groups/combustion/sdmech/sandiego20161214/sandiego20160815_trans.txt (thermo for these species from Cantera's n-hexane-NUIG-2015.yaml)

radiation.source: TNF Workshop radiation model, https://tnfworkshop.org/radiation/ (RADCAL fits, Grosshandler NIST TN 1402; Barlow et al. 2001 Combust. Flame 127:2102). a_p in 1/(m atm), valid 300-2500 K, a_p = sum c_k (1000/T)^k

sources.rho_s_kg_m3,cp_s_kJ_kgK,k_s_W_mK,dh_c_MJ: Carmignani, PhD dissertation 'Opposed-Flow Flame Spread over Solid Fuels in Different Burning Regimes' (UCSD/SDSU 2019), Table A.1, https://escholarship.org/content/qt0rb693zc/qt0rb693zc.pdf
sources.T_v_K,L_gasif_kJ_kg,B_air: Zhang et al., J. Fire Sciences 32(1) 2014 52-71, Table 1 (properties from Ahmad and Faeth), https://www.grace.umd.edu/~pbs/2014%20Zhang%20et%20al.%20JFS.pdf

sources.area_density_mg_cm2,cotton_area_density_: Olson et al., 'The effect of duct size, sample size, and fuel composition on concurrent flame spread over large cellulose samples in microgravity' (accepted manuscript), https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/id/eprint/10164340/
sources.half_area_density_g_cm2,cp_cotton_J_gK,c: same paper: 'initial half-thickness area density ... 0.009 g/cm2', 'fiberglass (0.7 J/g K) and cotton (1.26 J/g K)', 'Lv=300+(Cp,f - Cs)(Ts-300) J/g', 'plateaued ... at the 400 C pyrolysis temperature'
sources.thickness_mm: Zhao, T'ien, Ferkul, Olson, 9th US National Combustion Meeting 2015, NTRS 20150008962: 'thickness of the sample is about 0.32 mm with an area density 18.2 mg/cm2'

gas_for_spread.source: Carmignani dissertation (2019), Table A.1 gas column and Sec. 3.2.1: F 'varying between 4.4 and 5.5', good agreement for thin fuels 'when F = 4.76'
